vila-flor.name: Vila Flor Palace and Cultural Centre
vila-flor.short: An 18th-century palace and a 2005 cultural centre by Pitágoras Arquitectos, with an 800-seat hall
vila-flor.long: The Vila Flor Palace was built in the 18th century for Tadeu Luís António Lopes de Carvalho de Fonseca e Camões, and the Jordão family completed it. In 1853 Queen Maria II stayed here and, by decree of 23 June, raised Guimarães from a town to a city; in 1884 the palace hosted the city's first industrial and commercial exhibition. The municipality bought it in 1976. In 2005, following a competition, Pitágoras Arquitectos restored the palace and gardens and added a new building: the centre opened on 17 September with a Madredeus concert. The main hall seats about 800, the small hall 200, and the exhibition area is about 1,000 m².
vila-flor.history:
The Vila Flor Palace was built in the 18th century for Tadeu Luís António Lopes de Carvalho de Fonseca e Camões; it later passed to the Jordão family, who completed the work he had begun. The building became a landmark in the city's history. In 1853 Queen Maria II stayed at the palace: by a decree of 23 June that year she raised the then town of Guimarães to the status of a city. In 1884 the palace hosted the first Industrial and Commercial Exhibition of Guimarães.

The palace's box-hedged gardens, with a privileged view over the city, the Palace of the Dukes of Braganza and the castle, were the setting for important events: as early as 1750 the celebrations for the acclamation of King José I were held here. In 1976 the Guimarães municipality bought the palace, and the building was put to public use: it housed the Guimarães branch of the University of Minho, a music academy, a theatre workshop and vocational training courses. Part of the gardens was then used as the municipal plant nursery.

The Vila Flor Cultural Centre grew out of the restoration of the palace and its gardens and the construction of a new building for the performance hall. The municipality awarded the work through an open competition to the practice Pitágoras Arquitectos. The large new theatre building is combined with the 18th-century Baroque palace and its gardens. The centre opened on 17 September 2005 with a concert by Madredeus. It has a main hall of about 800 seats and a small hall of 200, and the new building also houses a restaurant, a café-concert and the administrative offices. The restored palace, with about 1,000 m² of exhibition space, also holds the Municipal Assembly.

The restored gardens of the cultural centre received an Honourable Mention in the public open spaces category of the 2006 National Landscape Architecture Prize. In 2012 Guimarães was a European Capital of Culture; a red heart sculpture in front of the palace is a reminder of it.

Today Vila Flor is the city's main cultural venue, hosting concerts, theatre and dance, exhibitions and festivals. It is run by the cultural cooperative A Oficina.

vila-flor.tip: The centre stands on Avenida D. Afonso Henriques, a ten-minute walk from the historic centre. Check the programme of plays and concerts at ccvf.pt; the box office is open on performance days. The palace rooms and gardens are open during opening hours; the red heart sculpture "Guimarães 2012" stands in front of the palace. There are views over the Palace of the Dukes of Braganza and the castle. Pair it with a walk through the gardens and to the Toural square.
